target.name: Orangewood Labs
target.founder: Abhinav Das, Aditya Bhatia, Akash Bansal

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $5M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Orangewood Labs is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $5M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies—1 public and 8 private—including Series B-stage robotics firms such as Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B), alongside earlier-stage players like Walden Robotics ($1.1B).

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, anchoring to the $5M raised as a proxy for post-seed value and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier for Series A progression, yields $10M. The peer-median method across the four sampled comparables—filtered to same sector and same/adjacent stage—produces $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.1B (floor) to $2.0B (ceiling). The wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in peer staging and maturity within the robotics sector.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $8.5M to $2.0B, with a median of $855M. The substantial gap between the stage-progression result and peer-median reflects the early-stage nature of Orangewood Labs relative to most sampled peers. Key uncertainties include whether the peer set—dominated by Series B companies—appropriately anchors a Series A valuation, and whether robotics sector multiples remain stable amid current market conditions. A tighter range would require additional data on Orangewood's revenue traction, unit economics, or pipeline maturity.
